title: Why BART reopened its check on union stewards’ paid time

beats.text: Two union representatives left their regular BART worksites before their shifts ended.

visual.sub: Three clock entries prompted a check of what the labor agreement allowed

beats.text: Supervisors entered end times in advance on three occasions.

visual.kicker: Three clock entries prompted a check of what the labor agreement allowed

beats.text: Investigators checked nine months of Fridays for 10 employees.
The 2022 report found the Friday time-theft allegation unsubstantiated.

visual.kicker: Investigators did not substantiate the Friday time-theft allegation

beats.text: The labor agreement allows paid time for authorized union work.

visual.kicker: Investigators did not substantiate the Friday time-theft allegation

beats.text: New reporting codes took effect in January 2024.

visual.kicker: New time codes led the office to close the recommendation

beats.text: The inspector general marked the recommendation implemented.

visual.kicker: New time codes led the office to close the recommendation

beats.text: But a new check of 2025 timesheets found missing codes and incomplete comments.

visual.kicker: A test of 2025 timesheets reopened the finding

beats.text: In May 2026 the inspector general reopened the recommendation.
The report did not publish an error rate or an amount of unauthorized pay.

visual.kicker: A test of 2025 timesheets reopened the finding

beats.text: BART set November 30 as its target to begin periodic audits.

visual.kicker: BART planned another round of payroll checks

beats.text: The public register still listed the work in progress a week before that date.
